SELECT state,
       SUM(total_offenses) AS total_rapes,
       SUM(cleared_A + cleared_B + cleared_C + cleared_D + cleared_E) AS cleared_exceptional,
       ROUND(100.0 * SUM(cleared_A + cleared_B + cleared_C + cleared_D + cleared_E) / NULLIF(SUM(total_offenses), 0), 1) AS exceptional_clearance_rate
FROM rollup.state_summary_clearance_detail
WHERE ucr_offense_code IN ('11A', '11B', '11C')
  AND year = 2025
GROUP BY state
HAVING SUM(total_offenses) >= 100
ORDER BY exceptional_clearance_rate DESC
LIMIT 20

observed.answer:
States ranked by the percentage of reported rapes cleared by exceptional means in 2025, restricted to states with at least 100 reported offenses. Under FBI definitions, an exceptional clearance occurs when law enforcement identifies the offender and establishes probable cause, but cannot make an arrest due to circumstances beyond their control (such as victim cooperation declining or the death of the offender). Note that 2025 data may be preliminary, and NIBRS reporting completeness varies across states.

Clearance note: FBI clearance means cleared by arrest or exceptional means; it is not the same as conviction or prosecution.

Ranking result limit: 20 rows.

Note: This data comes from the FBI's NIBRS program. Not all agencies report to this system, and some may have incomplete data — especially in their first year of NIBRS reporting or for recent months of data. Always verify that reported offenses are not impacted by incomplete coverage.
